newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Briton jailed for promoting child sex tours.
newsitem.headline: Briton jailed for promoting child sex tours.

text.p: A Briton accused of boasting that sex with a 12-year-old was as cheap as a hamburger was convicted of promoting child prostitution on Friday and sentenced to 16 years in prison.

In sentencing Michael Clarke, Judge Fatima Asdala also ordered the 48-year-old travel agent from Eastbourne deported from the Philippines immediately after completing his sentence and barred him from ever returning.
"I am completely innocent of this charge... It is absolutely diabolical. I've suffered enough," Clarke told reporters after the sentence.
"I shall be mounting a very strong appeal against this decision," he said, insisting the evidence against him had been fabricated.

According to evidence during the trial, Clarke published posters and brochures promoting his "Paradise Express" business which showed young boys and girls in sexually provocative poses and promising "outrageous happenings".
Although they did not specifically mention sex with minors, this literature referred to "young ladies ready for mounting".
A key witness against Clarke was another Briton, Martin Cottingham, a senior press officer for London-based charity Christian Aid.

Cottingham told the court at the start of Clarke's trial last month that the travel agent had promised him sex with an under-age girl and had advised him to bring a camera, video recorder and "fetish gear" to the Philippines.
Another witness also spoke of Clarke saying sex with a 12-year-old girl cost as much as a hamburger.
Clarke was alleged to have run his business in Olongapo, north of Manila, and nearby Angeles, towns with flourishing sex industries that used to be centred on U.S. military bases.
Friday's conviction was the latest volley in what has become an international crusade against paedophiles.
The Philippines earlier this year sentenced an Australian and a Briton to up to 17 years in jail each and several other foreigners are currently awaiting trial.
Philippine investigators have been receiving training from both British and Australian police in tackling sex crimes involving children.
A court in the Netherlands on Tuesday sentenced a man to five years in jail for what the judge described as "extraordinarily sickening" sex acts with children in the Philippines.

The Netherlands is one of several nations which have passed laws allowing their courts to punish padeophiles for offences committed overseas. Australian and German courts have jailed men for similar offences.
An Olongapo charity foundation which has been in the forefront of the campaign against paedophilia said Clarke's conviction demonstrated the progress the Philippines had made.

"This conviction shows how far the national government's attitudes and that of the judiciary have changed in the past few years when there was an attitude of cover-up, non-enforcement and denial of child sex abuse," the PREDA foundation said.
